title: Clinical examination: systems, sequence and closure
subject: emergency
summary: Consent, hygiene, positioning and dignified exposure open every examination, with chaperone for intimate parts. Systems are examined in protective sequence and always compared: pulses bilaterally, chest signs combined, abdomen inspected and auscultated before palpation, motor power with tone and reflexes. Closure summarises findings, differentials, targeted tests and safety netting.

sections.title: Open
items: Consent, hand hygiene, positioning, exposure with dignity and chaperone where intimate examination is involved.
Approach the painful area last in abdomen, joint and breast examination.

sections.title: Systems
items: Cardiovascular: compare both radial pulses, radio femoral delay, pressure, jugular venous pulse and auscultation as one set.
Respiratory: expansion, percussion, breath sounds and vocal resonance compared on both sides.
Abdomen: inspection, auscultation, percussion, then palpation. Joints: look, feel, active then passive move, stability and neurovascular check.
Thyroid and nodes: gland plus systemic signs, swallowing and tongue movement; nodes by site, size, consistency, tenderness, mobility, skin and drainage area.

sections.title: Close
items: Summarise findings, state likely differentials with honest uncertainty, thank the patient, and agree targeted investigations and safety netting.
Record findings in anatomical language the next clinician can relocate.
